_comment: Canonical Thai glossary. This is the reference layer: names are written in
their complete reviewed form without shortening them for a ROM field.
tools/build_script_glossary.py merges this file with the extracted pilot and
unit catalog, then applies translations/rom-glossary.th.json only when a
measured ROM field genuinely needs a shorter display form.
Spellings follow how these series are read in Thai fan translation, not a
romanisation table: มาซินก้า not มาจินก้า, ชาร์ not ชะอะ, กันดั้ม not กันดามุ.
Where a Thai reader knows a term in Latin letters (GP-01, EN, SP) it stays
Katakana proper names are transliterated from their reference-language
reading; their semantic components are not translated unless the project
has an explicitly reviewed canonical Thai name.
Groups starting with _ are notes, not substitutions.

_sources: Official English title/name forms: Super Robot Wars 30, Sunrise World,
L-Gaim official site, Gundam official material and King Records GoShogun.
SRW-original Latin spellings are cross-checked against Akurasu's master
character list. _name_sources is reference metadata and is never emitted
_voice: The user asked for manga/anime register, which in Thai is carried almost
entirely by pronouns. Japanese marks them and Thai marks them differently,
so they are chosen per speaker rather than per word:
オレ / 俺   hot-blooded lead      ฉัน   (Ryoma, Kouji, Judau, Masaki)
オレ / 俺   rough or villainous   ข้า   (Zeze-Nan, Guest commanders)
ボク / 僕   young or gentle       ผม    (Kamille, Shou, Kou, Seabook)
ワタシ / 私 officer, formal male  ผม    (Bright, Quattro, Amuro)
ワタシ / 私 female                ฉัน   (Emma, Sayla, Haman, Cham)
ワシ        elder                 ข้า   (Daisaku's uncle, Prof. Yumi)
お前 / キサマ  แก / เจ้า   depending on how hostile
あんた         นาย / เธอ
君             เธอ (to a peer) / นาย (to a subordinate)
あなた         คุณ
Rank stays: 大尉 เรืออากาศเอก, 中尉 เรืออากาศโท, 少尉 เรืออากาศตรี,
艦長 กัปตัน, 隊長 หัวหน้าหน่วย. Bright is เรืออากาศเอกไบรท์ on first
mention in a scene and just ไบรท์ afterwards, the way the dub does it.
Katakana used for emphasis rather than as a name — バカ ダメ ホント ムダ
ヤツ ウソ ヤバイ ムチャ ケンカ カタキ オヤジ ヤロー — is ordinary Thai
chosen for the moment (บ้า, ไม่ได้, จริงเหรอ, เปล่าประโยชน์, หมอนั่น,
โกหก, แย่แล้ว, บ้าบิ่น, ทะเลาะ, ศัตรูคู่แค้น, พ่อ/ไอ้แก่, ไอ้เวร) and is
deliberately not in the substitution table above.
_style: 「」 becomes nothing: Thai does not bracket speech, and the game already
shows who is speaking. The brackets are dropped, not replaced with " ".
・・・ becomes ... and stays where it was — the pauses are acting, and
cutting them flattens every hesitation in the game.
！！ becomes ! — Thai does not double it. ！？ becomes ?!
A line break in the source is a line break in the target. The window is
narrow, so a Thai line that runs long is rewritten shorter rather than
wrapped; tools/check_script.py reports any line that overruns.
